item.title: Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode Reduce Publisher Traffic
item.description:
Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode Reduce Publisher Traffic

Publishers spent years figuring out how to get clicks on Google, building a reciprocal relationship where they supplied content and Google supplied exposure. In 2024 and 2025 Google introduced AI‑driven search features that have reshaped that relationship and sharply lowered traffic to many news sites.

🔍 Overview

  • AI Overviews (2024) – An AI‑generated summary appears at the very top of Google Search, followed by links to sources the AI deems most useful. [Evidence]
  • AI Mode (May 2025) – Replaces standard search with a chatbot‑like interface that provides detailed summaries from web results. [Evidence]
  • The features change how results are ranked and displayed, making it harder for publishers to rely on Google traffic alone. [Evidence]

🗓️ Timeline

Year Feature Key Change
2024 AI Overviews AI‑generated summary placed at top of results with source links below.
2025 AI Mode Standard search replaced by a chatbot‑style interface that returns detailed summaries.

📉 Impact on Publishers

  • News outlets that spent time and money optimizing pages for clicks saw traffic tank after the AI features launched. [Evidence]
  • The Wall Street Journal (June 2025) reported declines for Business Insider, The Washington Post, HuffPost, and the WSJ itself since 2022. [Evidence]
  • Similarweb data showed The New York Times’ search traffic fell from 44 % to 35.5 % over three years. [Evidence]
  • DCN reported 19 members lost 1–25 % of Google traffic between May and June 2025. [Evidence]
  • DMG Media (Daily Mail, Metro) told the UK CMA click‑through rates dropped up to 89 % between June and July 2025, citing AI Overviews. [Evidence]
  • Pew Research found users are less likely to click on external links when an AI Overview is shown. [Evidence]
  • The News/Media Alliance warned AI Overviews would be “catastrophic” for web traffic. [Evidence]

🛠️ Google’s Response

  • Offered a toggle that lets sites opt out of appearing in AI Overviews and AI Mode without losing standard search visibility (rolled out after a UK order). [Evidence]
  • Made source links more prominent: hovering over a link shows a pop‑up with article titles and images. [Evidence]
  • Added another AI change that puts in‑line links higher up in responses more frequently. [Evidence]
  • Google’s leadership statements: Liz Reid said click volume remained “relatively stable,” while Nick Fox said “from our point of view, the web is thriving.” [Evidence]

⚖️ Legal and Regulatory Context

  • US District Judge Amit Mehta dismissed an antitrust suit from Chegg and Penske Media and rejected a class‑action claim from Arkansas newspapers over AI Overviews. [Evidence]
  • The UK Competition and Markets Authority received complaints from DMG Media about click‑through declines linked to AI Overviews. [Evidence]

The rollout of AI Overviews and AI Mode marks a significant shift in Google Search, turning a long‑standing traffic source into a more opaque AI‑mediated layer and prompting measurable traffic losses across the digital publishing ecosystem.

#GoogleAI #DigitalPublishing #SearchTraffic #AIOverviews

Source: Google’s AI search changes upended online publishing

item.title: Judge Dismisses Chegg and PMC Antitrust Lawsuits Over Google AI Search
item.description:
Judge Dismisses Chegg and PMC Antitrust Lawsuits Over Google AI Search

Federal Judge Amit Mehta dismissed the antitrust lawsuits brought by Chegg and Rolling Stone parent Penske Media Corporation, which alleged that Google’s AI‑powered search features siphoned traffic from their sites.

🔍 Overview

  • Chegg and PMC claimed Google abused monopoly power by coercing publishers into providing content for AI Overviews for free, or risk disappearing from search results.
  • The lawsuits, filed last year, asserted that Google’s AI search features diverted traffic away from publishers, hurting revenue.

⚖️ Legal Ruling

  • Judge Mehta wrote that the plaintiffs’ claims “don’t stand up to antitrust law.”
  • He noted the plaintiffs have only “pleaded an ‘expectation’ that Google will send them search traffic if they make their content available for free.”
  • “But an expectation is not an agreement. It is simply how a general search engine works,” Mehta wrote.
  • The court is “not ‘unsympathetic to the situation publishers now find themselves in,’” but said antitrust rules cannot replace legislative action on the economic impact of “new innovation.”

📉 Impact on Publishers

  • Publishers continue to see a steep dive in traffic to news outlets and small websites after Google’s AI‑powered search overhaul.

💰 Google Pilot Payments

  • This week, The Information reported that Google is paying around 100 publishers for their contributions to AI Overviews, AI Mode, and Gemini as part of a pilot program.

Disclosure: The Verge is part of Penske Media.

#Google #Antitrust #AIOverviews

Source: Judge dismisses antitrust lawsuits over Google’s AI Overviews

item.title: Google Launches Pilot Program to Pay Publishers for AI Contributions
item.description:
Google Launches Pilot Program to Pay Publishers for AI Contributions

Google has introduced a pilot program that compensates publishers for their contributions to its AI-powered search features and chatbot, according to reports from Digiday and The Information.

⚙️ Key details

  • The program began less than a year ago.
  • Approximately 100 publishers have joined the pilot.
  • Payments are based on how much content contributed to:
    • AI Overviews
    • AI Mode in Search
    • Gemini chatbot

💰 Compensation Examples

Publisher Status Reported Earnings
Joined at program start Over $1 million in a year
Joined a few months ago Around $50,000 to $60,000

💡 Why it matters

Google is facing scrutiny regarding the impact of its AI features on web traffic. This comes alongside regulatory actions:

  • In June, the UK ruled that Google must allow publishers to opt out of appearing in AI search features.
  • The European Union has opened an investigation into the impact on web traffic and ordered Google to make changes to its search engine.

#Google #AI #Publishing #Gemini #Search

Source: Google reportedly tests paying publishers for AI search results
